column1: # gate-commands.tsv - the gate's command units: the checks that are not
# `go test` of one package (edition vet, golangci-lint, the web suites),
# declared once and run by `testrunner gate` on its workers through
# tools/testrunner/bootstrap.sh exec, in the source tree, under the run's
# test timeout. A command unit passes on exit 0 and fails otherwise, with its
# output tail in the summary. The commands are the repo's own: each row says
# where it was taken from, and a change there must be mirrored here.
# Columns (tab separated; '#' lines and blank lines are ignored):
#   name      the unit's id and ledger key. {set} and {shard} are filled in
#             by the expansion.
#   expand    -            one unit
#             omit-sets    one unit per tag set `scripts/omit-tag-check.sh
#                          --list-tests --scope distro` prints (the editions and
#                          no_obs, what ci.yml runs per push; `testrunner
#                          gate --omit-scope all` lists every set, the
#                          dispatched matrix); {set} in the command is the
#                          set, {set} in
#                          the name its key (a distro set's sbo_distro_*
#                          stamp, else the set), and the weight is the set's
#                          row in omit-tag-weights.tsv (else this row's)
#             packages:N   N units over every package of the main module
#                          (go list ./... as GOOS=linux), dealt by weight
#                          (go-test-weights.tsv) longest first; {packages}
#                          in the command is the shard's ./dir list, {shard}
#                          in the name is i/N, and each gets weight/N
#   when      on an affected gate the row runs when a changed file matches
#             one entry: *.ext (suffix), dir/ (prefix) or an exact path;
#             always on --full
#   tools     - or a comma list: node, golangci-lint (pinned in
#             gate-tools.tsv), own-tree (a fresh copy of the source for
#             a command that writes into the tree, so it never races the
#             other units of a multi-slot box; list it before git-index),
#             git-index (a git repository of the tree the command runs in,
#             for commands that call git)
#   weight_s  estimated seconds on a CI-sized runner (LPT order and the
#             spend projection only)
#   command   run by bash -c in the source tree
# vet: ci.yml's omit-tags job runs scripts/omit-tag-check.sh per set: go vet
#   -tags <set> ./..., plus the tagged packages' tests for the four editions.
#   The gate splits that in two so one edition is not one 20-minute unit:
#   this row runs the vet (--vet-only), and every package the editions test
#   (--list-tests) becomes a Go unit of its own run with -tags <set>
#   (<import>[<set key>], split like any Go unit at a quarter of its
#   split-table parts), triggered with this row. The script reads the tree
#   with git grep.
# lint: ci.yml's lint job (golangci-lint-action, version v2.14.0, default
#   args: golangci-lint run over ./...). Sharding by package keeps the
#   findings identical to the whole-tree run: every enabled linter analyses
#   one package at a time (facts from dependencies are computed either way),
#   the exclusions are path rules, and .golangci.yml sets no per-run issue
#   limits (max-issues-per-linter and max-same-issues are 0). The shards
#   together list exactly the packages ./... matches.
# web: ci.yml's frontend job (web) and ci-private.yml's frontend-web2 job
#   (web2), step by step, including their embedded-dist drift checks;
#   webcloud: the webcloud step of ci.yml's taxonomy-build-drift job (npm ci,
#   then make verify-webcloud-dist, which runs this script). shared/ has no
#   suite of its own; the three apps import it, so a shared/ change runs all
#   three.
vet:{set}
lint:{shard}
web:web
column6: cd web && npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && cd .. && node scripts/uicopylint/uicopylint.mjs web/src && cd web && npm run build && cd .. && scripts/sync-web-embed.sh web/dist internal/intelligence/dashboard/webapp/dist && { drift=$(git status --porcelain -- internal/intelligence/dashboard/webapp/dist); [ -z "$drift" ] || { echo "Committed webapp/dist drifted from web/dist. Run make web-build and commit the result."; echo "$drift" | head -40; exit 1; }; }

Run make web-build-org and commit the result."; echo "$drift" | head -40; exit 1; }; }

column1: # migcheck: internal/migcheck's online migration rules (plan 06 18.2.4) over
#   the org PostgreSQL and cloud lineages; the pre-push hook runs it advisory.
#   Advisory here too until R1: it flips to --enforce at R1, when the M0.8
#   rules land in CLAUDE.md and M3a ships the non-transactional step class
migcheck
# orgstateinv: the org server's process-wide state against tools/orgstateinv/allowlist.tsv
#   (plan 07 M2.1). Its test reads the tree from disk, so cipkgs does not select it
#   on an org-server change; this row does.
orgstateinv
# structcheck: the managed-SaaS structural rules (plan 07 M3-0.8; tools/structcheck/doc.go
#   lists them): tenancy classes, new-table org_id, raw advisory locks, package state,
#   root files, imports_test pins and lease_gen are enforced; RLS policies, ON CONFLICT
#   targets and plan-name literals are advisory until M3b.1, M3a.4 and internal/entitlements.
#   S9 reads every package directory under internal/, hence the broad when.
structcheck
# opsgate: the Track E gate driver, the nightly and the train (plan 07 M11.2a, M11.2b, M11.3, M11.4; deploy/saas-ovh/ops,
#   deploy/saas-ovh/roll.sh). test-ops.sh runs nightly.sh against a throwaway git history with a built gatedriver, a
#   stubbed systemctl and a fake bisect runner (a seeded failure is named), and bash -n (shellcheck when installed) on
#   every ops script; test-roll.sh runs roll.sh's dry run and its promote, halt and inconclusive paths with stubbed
#   ssh, curl and judge. The Go rules are the tools/gatedriver and internal/trainhalt Go units.
opsgate
# drift: ci-private.yml's generated-file drift jobs that need only go, git and make
#   (L-139: the v1.39.0 release found stale OpenAPI stubs and a stale track sitemap
#   that no gate row had checked). Not here: the website accuracy check (it reads the
#   GitHub API) and verify-distribution-readmes (it needs python3, absent from the
#   golang image); the release preflight runs both. Nor verify-track-build: its
#   sitemap <lastmod> dates come from `git log`, and the git-index snapshot is one
#   commit made today, so every page would read as changed (ci-private.yml's
#   track-build-drift job keeps running it on GitHub). verify-docs-build masks the
#   two git-derived page dates for the same reason, so it runs here; docs/sdk/ and
#   shared/lib/productNames.json are in `when` because gen publishes the first
#   (nav.toml [roots] sdk) and expands @@name@@ tokens from the second. git-index: the
#   scripts start with git rev-parse --show-toplevel.
drift
column6: make verify-openapi verify-website-build verify-docs-build verify-w8-claims verify-adapter-parity-doc verify-guard-coverage-ts

website-tests
# sdk: the SDK matrix (plan W2-4 and principle 9, lane B4): sdk/python on
#   every CPython its requires-python admits (3.9 to 3.13) and sdk/typescript
#   on Node 20, 22 and 24 (Node 18 dropped: past end of life), each on the runtime pinned in gate-tools.tsv;
#   sdk:pack builds the release artifacts exactly as sdk-release.yml does
#   (scripts/ci/sdk.sh pack); sdk:e2e is the contract suite against a real
#   machine and a real org gateway (tests/sdke2e: builds observer and
#   observer-org, starts both on scratch ports with a private PostgreSQL,
#   runs both SDKs' example apps to the local, online and both destinations
#   and checks the spans landed with identity, tokens and cost). sdk.sh
#   copies the package into the unit's TMPDIR, so the units share the tree
#   safely. sdk:e2e needs PostgreSQL 16 binaries on the worker (initdb,
#   pg_ctl; on PATH or under /usr/lib/postgresql/*/bin), or a server named
#   by OBSERVER_CONTROL_STORE_DSN.

sdk:python-3.10
sdk:python-3.11
sdk:python-3.12
